memory_update.text: FLS is a strong underfollowed candidate for the nuclear-qualified components node because it has explicit ASME N/NPT/NA, NQA-1, Appendix B-related qualifications and nuclear pumps/valves/seals exposure, while public-market labeling remains general industrial flow control.

MG is a small-cap underfollowed service candidate for nuclear inspection/NDT/outage work, but nuclear revenue materiality is not yet proven and must be verified before advancing beyond hypothesis status.

CW and BWXT should remain reference anchors for nuclear-qualified components/services; both are more visible and larger-cap than the target discovery profile but define the quality-assurance and installed-base benchmark.

The chokepoint appears less about generic industrial equipment and more about qualified nuclear QA systems, ASME/NQA certifications, Appendix B compliance, installed-base documentation, utility acceptance, and outage execution capability.

Need next-pass verification from ASME certificate-holder database, NRC/vendor qualification references, and company filings to distinguish true nuclear revenue exposure from marketing-page optionality.

summary: Expanded the node into a two-lane universe of US-listed direct-exposure companies. Reference lane includes established nuclear component leaders with visible commercial and/or naval nuclear exposure. Underfollowed lane includes smaller or less narratively crowded suppliers/service providers where ASME/NQA qualification, inspection know-how, installed-base service, and outage/refueling demand may be the actual chokepoint. This is a research universe only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
